description: Figure 10, titled “The effect of context masking on case tasks groupby by language family. Error bars indicate the standard deviation,” is a bar chart that visualizes the impact of context masking on model performance across case-related tasks, aggregated by language family. The horizontal axis lists distinct language families (e.g., Indo-European, Uralic, Altaic, etc.), while the vertical axis represents the magnitude of the effect, likely measured as a change in accuracy or loss, though the exact unit is not specified in the visible caption. Each language family is represented by a single bar, with error bars extending vertically from the top of each bar to indicate the standard deviation of the measured effect across tasks or models within that family. The bars vary in height, suggesting that the effect of context masking is not uniform across language families — some families show a larger degradation in performance (taller bars), while others show minimal impact (shorter bars). The chart appears to be sorted in descending order of effect size, with the most affected families on the left. No color coding or grouping is evident; all bars are rendered in a uniform style, emphasizing the comparative magnitude of the perturbation effect per language family. The presence of error bars highlights the variability in the effect within each group, indicating that while trends are observable, there is some statistical uncertainty in the measurements.
